methodology: Curated, directly linked public original sources. Report statistics come from different release vintages and are not institution fraud losses. Researchers should confirm source revisions and reporting periods. Not an exhaustive literature review.

reports.title: CAFC Fraud Reporting System open dataset
reports.coverage: 2021 through September 2025 in the currently linked CSV
reports.why: Province, fraud typology, reports, victim counts and monetary loss; analyze geographic and type trends
reports.limitations: Self-reported records; Q4 2025 delayed owing to a system transition; not institution-owned bank losses

reports.title: 2024 Annual Statistical Report
reports.why: Fraud types, province-level reporting, age breakdown and payment/solicitation methods
reports.limitations: Reports to the CAFC, not a census of incidents; figures may later be revised

reports.title: 2022 Annual Report
reports.why: Fraud typologies, victim loss changes, payment and solicitation patterns
reports.limitations: Reported losses and cases, not actual total prevalence

reports.title: 2021 Annual Report
reports.why: Pre- and early-pandemic changes in scam tactics and reported losses
reports.limitations: Underreporting; figures may be adjusted in later publications

reports.title: 2024 CSA Investor Index
reports.why: Investor behavior, exposure to investment scams, social-media and self-directed investment patterns
reports.limitations: Survey results, not recorded confirmed fraud incidents

reports.title: 2024 Investor Index: Investment fraud and social media trends
reports.why: 23% of Canadians surveyed reported encountering possible fraudulent investments
reports.limitations: Encountering a possible scam differs from being a victim or proving wrongdoing

reports.title: 2025 Annual Report — Consumer banking fraud complaints
reports.publisher: Ombudsman for Banking Services and Investments
reports.why: 1,815 fraud-related banking investigations, up from 966 in 2024; analyze disputes and resolution patterns
reports.limitations: Complaint investigations, not proven bank breaches or annual bank-owned fraud losses

reports.title: OBSI response to National Anti-Fraud Strategy consultation
reports.publisher: Ombudsman for Banking Services and Investments
reports.why: Links scam typologies, disputed e-transfers and customer redress into process-improvement questions
reports.limitations: Policy recommendations and service experience, not adjudicated bank misconduct

reports.title: Why speaking up about fraud matters
reports.why: Consumer survey exposure to investment fraud, unauthorized card use and phishing
reports.limitations: Self-reported survey measures differ from CAFC case data

reports.title: FCAC briefing to Senate Banking Committee
reports.why: Reported loss figures, underreporting and digital fraud patterns
reports.limitations: Briefing data may reflect subsequent revisions

reports.title: Self-reported fraud in Canada, 2019
reports.why: Population prevalence and underreporting beyond police-recorded cases
reports.limitations: Survey of 2019 experiences, not current fraud incidence

reports.title: Police-reported crime statistics in Canada, 2024
reports.why: Police-reported fraud, identity theft, extortion and cyber components
reports.limitations: Not directly comparable to CAFC consumer self-reports; local police coverage differences

reports.title: Police-reported crime statistics in Canada, 2025
reports.why: Fraud and extortion changes, police-reported rates and decade-long comparisons
reports.limitations: Police-reported rate is not a population victimization survey or a count of bank failures

reports.title: Fraud Prevention Month 2024: 2023 Canadian reported-loss update
reports.why: Source for roughly C$567 million in victim-reported losses for 2023
reports.limitations: Published in 2024 and can differ from later revised totals

reports.title: Fraud Prevention Month: 2025 reported Canadian losses
reports.why: C$704 million-plus reported victim losses and low reporting rates
reports.limitations: CAFC victim reports, not direct institutional losses

reports.title: 2025 Assessment of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risks in Canada
reports.why: FinCrime typology context linking fraud-generated proceeds to AML risk
reports.limitations: National assessment, not bank-specific wrongdoing or attributable individual losses
